authored_from.text: Hand-written from docs/specs/SPEC-14-automated-crew-training.md (S14-R1..R7, S14-AC1..AC4, AC6) and the worlds in this file, before any training-v2 code exists. training-v2 traces state what the spec requires of each world; training-v1 control traces state what the v1 rules require (roles by exact crew name from sdk/training/strategy.py DEFAULT_ROLES, tier bands by stat total over capacity, the Fitness 101 gate for primary T1, an explicit zero declared cost, one start per idle crew, UncertainPriorAttemptError after an unknown attempt). No expected value was produced by running the code under test.
interpretations: I1 Role assignment (S14-R1): first assign as many distinct requested specialist slots (repair, shields, weapons) as the roster supports, then maximise the sum of the assigned crew's stats in their roles; equal scores go to the lower instance id. A role no crew can fill is reported role_uncovered.

I2 Role words map to stats repair=Repair, shields=Science, weapons=Weapon (vocabulary.roles). A crew can fill a role when that stat is observed, an observed 0 included: an observed 0 is never unknown. A stat missing from the reply is unknown, never 0; S14-R1 lets the planner either skip such a crew (stats_unknown) or estimate the missing stat from design and level (observed stats preferred), so no trace freezes either choice for a crew with a missing stat (alternatives are listed with any_of where the choice changes the plan).

I3 At most one training start per account per run (S14-Q1): a dry run journals at most one add_training per account, and an execute sends at most one AddTraining per account, whichever of several eligible crew it picks unless the trace names the winner (candidate_one_of otherwise).

I4 Training is planned after the progression block (S14 Interfaces): an earlier upgrade's spend counts against the balance, the authorization's per-account spend caps and the registry's max_actions before a training start.

I5 Previews (crew-plan, dry-run) need no provisioned attempt store. An execute needs one provisioned explicitly (step kind provision) and refuses with state_missing otherwise; it never creates or recreates the store itself.

I6 A refusal inside a run is a skip with exit 0 unless the trace says otherwise; a refusal before login exits nonzero. A disabled account (registry enabled false) is not run at all: zero requests, no code required.

I7 Eligibility from fresh reads (S14-R2): room status Normal, the course's room type and level, room capacity (running sessions in the room below Capacity), required research Completed, no running or unclaimed course, observed fatigue below 100 (fatigued otherwise), training points (the sum of the nine stats) below the design's training capacity (tp_cap_reached otherwise).

I8 Price (S14-R4): CostString '<currency>:<amount>'; absent -> price_unavailable, unparseable -> price_malformed, starbux -> premium_currency, above the balance -> insufficient_funds, above the remaining authorization cap -> cap_exceeded; an explicitly observed 0 is accepted. Each scenario has exactly one valid code.

I9 Verification (S14-R5): verified only from a fresh roster read after the start showing the requested course with a running timer. A different course, a roster that lacks the character, a failed post-read or a lost reply leave the attempt unresolved (journal outcome unknown, not-observed or contradicted unless the trace pins one) and block every later start on the account, another crew included, until an operator resolution (step kind resolve) records a durable reconciliation; the next execute may then start one eligible crew.

I10 After sending, the pending record survives every failure. A lost AddTraining reply with failing post-reads keeps the attempt store present and journals the attempt unresolved. A settle write that fails after an applied start (SETTLE_WRITE_HOOK) also keeps the store present, the start applied once, so the next execute (after a fresh dry run) sends no AddTraining and reports unresolved_attempt. An intent that cannot be persisted sends nothing (intent_not_persisted).

I11 Overlapping dispatches of one identity: the lock holder starts at most one eligible crew (either), the other dispatch sends no account write and reports locked; a separate account starts independently.

I12 The operator stop control: a STOP file present before the run refuses before login; a STOP file created during the run stops the account before its training start, recorded with status or reason 'stopped'.
I13 A crew in a non-training room keeps its role in the crew plan and is skipped not_in_training_room; it is not moved (relocation is out of scope).
I14 Research unobserved (the ship read omits Researches) -> research_unknown and the dry run plans nothing.

I15 'A matching recent dry run' (S14-R4): every execute after an earlier execute or resolve runs right after a fresh dry-run step (world edits aside), so the traces hold under either reading, SPEC-05's completed dry run of the same registry and policy within 24 hours, or a dry run that planned this very start. A dry run is a read-only preview: it completes (exit 0) for an account blocked by an unresolved attempt, and the execute run reports the block.

I16 A course's room level is a minimum (S14-R2 'matches room level'): a course of level n can be taken in a training room of level n or more, so a level-1 course trains in a level-2 Academy, and never in a lower one.

I17 A locked account (an overlapping dispatch of the same identity holds its lock) is skipped, not stopped or failed: it does not count toward the fleet halt share (DEFAULT_HALT_SHARE 0.0 in sdk/fleet/factory.py halts on any stopped account), so the dispatch goes on to its other accounts.

vocabulary.matching: A skip matches only in a structured record of that account: a run-record account entry (status, reason, results reasons, rejected candidates and reasons), a journal event (reason and params), or a pre-login refusal line "  - account '<alias>': ..." naming exactly one code; the crew's seeded instance id must be in the same record when the expectation names a crew. Free stdout never matches a skip. A crew-plan entry matches one stdout line holding the crew's instance id, the role word and the course name or exactly one skip code. A prestige entry matches one stdout line holding the target and ingredient design names and 'missing <n>'. Step kinds provision and resolve, the attempt store's location and the intent-write hook are interface assumptions pinned in scripts/training_workflow_benchmark.py (INTERFACE ASSUMPTIONS), never here.

cases.summary: A roster without any original target name gets distinct repair, weapons and shields specialists; swapping two crew members' stats swaps their roles. Both previews agree and neither mutates.

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --crew-plan is not implemented

cases.summary: The crew plan shows the direct Prestige route to an original named target (Galactic Succubus from two Synthetic Cadets) with one missing when the roster has one copy, reports uncovered roles, and labels research unknown when the ship read omits it. Neither preview mutates.

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --crew-plan is not implemented

cases.summary: An idle repair specialist in a ready level 2 Academy with a 500-mineral Engineering Manual: exactly 500 spendable starts it and charges 500; 499, an earlier reservation, a premium price or an unavailable price start nothing; an explicitly observed zero price starts it for free. Spend above the authorization cap, or above the cap or action budget an earlier upgrade left, starts nothing.

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --fleet-provision-training is not implemented (exit 2)

cases.summary: The dry run and the execute plan see an eligible start; just after the execute run's first roster read the room starts upgrading, the crew moves out, the research disappears or the price rises. The preflight recheck from fresh reads sends nothing. A full Academy, a crew at its training-point capacity, or a crew that becomes fatigued after the first read starts nothing.

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --fleet-provision-training is not implemented (exit 2)

cases.summary: A fresh read with the requested course and timer verifies a start. An active course, a missing or stale dry run, a missing authorization or a disabled account start nothing. A different course or a missing post-read leaves an unresolved attempt that blocks the next run even for another eligible crew member. A post-read that lacks the character's id is unresolved too; an operator resolution lifts the block and the next run starts exactly one eligible crew. The disabled account's dry run first shows training-v2 accepted.

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --fleet-provision-training and --fleet-resolve-training are not implemented (exit 2)

cases.summary: A crash after sending (applied) or before the server applied, and an intent store that cannot be written, all leave the next run with no training start, even with a different crew member eligible. A lost AddTraining reply with failing post-reads (lost-reply-failed-post-read) leaves only the original request and a durable pending record that blocks the rerun; a settle write that fails after an applied start (settle-write-fails) keeps the pending intent, so the next execute sends nothing (unresolved_attempt).

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --fleet-provision-training is not implemented (exit 2)

cases.summary: Two execute dispatches for the same account overlap behind a barrier at login. The holder of the account's dispatch lock sends at most one start; the other sends no account write at all, although a different crew member is eligible.

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --fleet-provision-training is not implemented (exit 2): no dispatch logs in, so the barrier and hold witnesses are missing

cases.summary: One dispatch holds alpha's lock at its paid start while a second dispatch of the same two-account registry skips alpha as locked and still makes bravo's paid start in bravo's own world; every request and journal entry stays with its own account.

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --fleet-provision-training is not implemented (exit 2): no dispatch logs in, so the barrier and hold witnesses are missing

cases.summary: The fleet stop file refuses before login. A removed or unreadable established attempt store stops execution instead of being recreated as a fresh account. A legacy-run account that is only serialized, not skipped, is refused. The stop scenarios first show training-v2 accepted; a stop file created during the run stops the account; an execute before explicit provisioning refuses (state_missing) and creates no store.

red.expected_cause: registry refuses training-v2 before login (exit 2); --fleet-provision-training is not implemented (exit 2); no scenario passes: each stop scenario first needs an accepted training-v2 dry run
